title: Stochastic quantization paths benchmarking
body:
Purpose and quick summary:

This working note documents an exploratory benchmark series that looks at the *stochastic paths* quantizers take during per-layer/noise-aware calibration and how path variability interacts with kernel selection at runtime. The goal: characterize when stochastic quantization (randomized rounding, sample-based activation statistics) causes reproducible latency/throughput jitter or systematic quality drift compared to deterministic post-training quant (GPTQ/AWQ) across different kernels.

Why this is different from our previous sweeps:
- Prior work focused on mean quality/latency tradeoffs for specific quant recipes; this doc focuses on variance and tail effects that cause intermittent SLA violations.
- We intentionally flip the random seed across runs to measure path-space instability rather than single-run averages.
- We test kernel families with differing vectorization and tiling behaviors to see whether kernel internals amplify stochastic artifacts.

Hardware / models / test harness:
- HW: H100 80GB (nvlink disabled) and A100 40GB nodes. Runs repeated on both archs when feasible.
- Models: Llama-2-13B-chat (hf converted), phi-7B-lite (compact transformer), and a distilled 3B internal eval model (text-class).
- Quant configs: GPTQ (deterministic per-layer rounding), AWQ (awq-v2 noise-aware), INT8 symmetric, FP8-e4m3 (framework emulation), and stochastic-INT8 (randomized rounding during calibration, 50 seeds per run).
- Kernels: kernel-vec-v1 (baseline vectorized matmul), kernel-tiling-v3 (aggressive tiling, prefetch heuristics), kernel-block-mono (block-based, lower memory overhead).
- Batch shapes: single-shot interactive (batch=1, seq=128), small batch (batch=4, seq=512), long context burst (batch=1, seq=2048).
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization, peak memory, end-to-end output quality metrics (perplexity on evaluation set, perplexity delta vs float32, and a small instruction-following accuracy probe). We also capture KL divergence of token distributions vs float baseline for a 200-sample subset.

Experiment design notes (procedural):
- For stochastic quant runs we run 50 independent calibrations (different random seeds) and push each compiled artifact through the exact same traffic replay trace (replayer v0.9).
- We pin scheduler settings to remove autoscaling noise and force single-model, single-stream infer loops on a reserved node to remove infra jitter.
- Kernel choice is forced at the runtime layer (explicit kernel selection flag) so we can attribute performance differences to kernel internals, not autoscheduler decisions.
- Each run captured with our microtrace collector and the lightweight profiler (trace window 20s warmup + 60s steady).

Key observations (high level):
1) Variance of quality is quant-config dependent: stochastic-INT8 shows a heavy tail in perplexity (top 5% seeds produce +7–12% perplexity relative to median) whereas GPTQ seeds cluster tightly (+1–2%). AWQ sits between (~+3–5% tail).
2) Kernel amplification: kernel-tiling-v3 amplifies worst-case quality drift for stochastic-INT8 by ~30% (relative to kernel-vec-v1) measured by KL divergence spikes. Hypothesis: tiling changes activation ordering and memory alignment causing different accumulator rounding accumulation paths which interact with randomized weight rounding.
3) Latency jitter correlates weakly with quality variance: some seeds produce both high perplexity and 1.6x p99 latency (on H100, long-context). Not universal — suggests orthogonal causes (e.g., kernel cache alignment w.r.t. KV cache sizes).
4) FP8 runs show relatively low variance on quality but uneven throughput on A100 (thermal throttling observed in one node — flagged separately).

Representative numbers (Llama-2-13B-chat, H100, batch=1, seq=128):
- float32 baseline throughput: 420 tok/s, p95 latency 75ms.
- GPTQ (kernel-vec-v1): median throughput 1250 tok/s, p95 18ms, perplexity delta +2.1%. seed variance ~0.4%.
- AWQ (kernel-vec-v1): median throughput 1300 tok/s, p95 17ms, perplexity delta +3.7%, seed tail up to +6.2%.
- stochastic-INT8 (kernel-vec-v1): median throughput 1275 tok/s, p95 19ms, perplexity delta median +4.1% but tail +12% at worst seeds.
- stochastic-INT8 (kernel-tiling-v3): median throughput 1200 tok/s, p95 22ms, worst-seed perplexity +15%.

Failure modes and oddities we want to highlight:
- Seed clustering: about ~10% of seeds for stochastic-INT8 produce pathological drift on models with larger layer-norm scale variance. This seems model-dependent.
- Kernel-tiling-v3 shows intermittent misaligned memcpy patterns (microtrace shows extra stall cycles on certain layer widths) which co-occur with quality spikes. Potential root cause: mispredicted prefetch leading to partial accumulation reorder.
- On A100, AWQ + kernel-block-mono sometimes drops throughput by ~18% under long contexts due to L2 thrash; not observed on H100.

Actions and next steps:
- Reproduce with controlled activation shuffles: add small deterministic permutation to activation layout during calibration to see if tiling sensitivity is purely memory-order related. (blocker: requires small runtime shim; PR candidate: PR #5278).
- Add seeded deterministic fallback: if stochastic calibration produces perplexity > threshold on small eval set, auto-run 3 additional seeds and pick median artifact. Measure cost tradeoff.
- Work with kernel team to add a diagnostic marker to tiling kernel to dump alignment and prefetch decisions when KL spike occurs.
- Expand coverage to 70B-class models (resource permitting) because worst tails may worsen with width.

Immediate TODOs (owners):
- Marisol: run activation shuffle experiments on H100 (ticket INF-2147).
- Daniel: instrument kernel-tiling-v3 with alignment dumps (PR review requested).
- Sofia: set up a lightweight QA probe that runs 8 seeds automatically and reports perplexity distribution to the console dashboard.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Is stochastic calibration useful in practice if we must run 3–5 seeds to get a safe median? At what point does cost negate benefit vs deterministic GPTQ?
- Can runtime routing decide kernel selection based on a "stability score" derived at compile time? What signals are reliable?
- How much of the observed effect is quantizer implementation detail vs fundamental to randomized rounding?

Notes / raw links to artifacts and scripts:
- bench harness: gs://redwood-bench/experiments/2028-11-stochastic-quant/run-harness.sh
- data: gs://redwood-bench/experiments/2028-11-stochastic-quant/results/*.json (seed-level outputs)
- profiler traces: gs://redwood-bench/experiments/2028-11-stochastic-quant/traces/

If you iterate on this doc, please add short changelog lines at the top with date and one-line summary so we track experiment forks.

End of note.
